examples.en: If you pay late, a surcharge is added.
If you have a certificate, you get bonus points.
An extra amount was added to the tax.
The amount rose a lot because an addition was applied.
Night work comes with an added allowance.

examples.ko: 이 경우에는 가산 없이 그대로 계산해요.
examples.en: In this case, we calculate it as it is, with nothing added.

explain: '가산'은 원래 금액이나 점수에 따로 더하는 것을 말해요. 일반 '더하기'가 아니라 규칙에 따라 붙는 추가분이라는 느낌이에요. '가산점', '가산세', '가산 수당'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '가산' is an amount or score added on top of the original one. Rather than plain addition, it feels like an extra portion applied by a rule. It forms terms like '가산점' (bonus points), '가산세' (penalty tax), and '가산 수당' (premium pay).

examples.en: How much is the gym's membership fee?
You pay the joining fee only once at the start.
The joining fee is free this month.
If you pay the joining fee, we give you a coupon.
The club's joining fee is 10,000 won.
I'm hesitating to join because of the joining fee.

explain: 모임이나 회원제에 처음 들어갈 때 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 달마다 내는 '회비', '월 이용료'와 달라요. '가입비 면제'나 '가입비 무료'는 광고에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It is the one-time payment when you first join a club or membership. It differs from '회비' or '월 이용료', which are paid regularly. '가입비 면제' and '가입비 무료' are common in ads.

examples.en: New students get their first-semester tuition reduced.
The city decided to reduce taxes for small business owners.
They reduce water bills for low-income households.

examples.ko: 올해부터 감면할 수 있는 세금이 늘었어요.
examples.en: From this year, more taxes can be reduced.

examples.ko: 서류를 내면 수업료를 감면받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you submit the documents, you can get your fees reduced.
They cut the parking fee for this month only.

explain: 세금, 등록금, 요금처럼 내야 하는 돈을 줄여 주거나 아예 안 받는다는 말이에요. 전부 안 내는 '면제하다'와 달리 일부를 줄여 주는 경우까지 넓게 써요. 혜택을 받는 사람은 '감면받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for money you owe, such as taxes, tuition and fees, when it is reduced or waived. Unlike '면제하다', which means not paying at all, it also covers partial reductions. The person receiving the benefit uses '감면받다'.

examples.en: I prepared documents to apply for a reduction in my insurance premium.
This reduction applies from next month.

examples.ko: 지원금 감액이 되면 생활이 많이 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If the subsidy is reduced, life gets much harder.

examples.ko: 감액에 이의가 있으면 이번 주 안에 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you object to the reduction, please tell us this week.
I was surprised that the reduction was bigger than I expected.
The reduced fine eased my burden a little.

explain: 보험료, 수당, 벌금처럼 정해진 돈의 액수를 줄이는 일이에요. 반대말은 '증액'이고, 공문서나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to lowering a fixed amount of money, such as insurance premiums, allowances or fines. Its opposite is '증액', and it often appears in official documents and the news.

en: be expensive; be valuable; be costly

examples.en: This painting is worth much more than I thought.
Don't put valuable items in your bag.
The ring my grandmother passed down was worth quite a lot.

examples.ko: 요즘 이 지역 땅은 값나가니까 팔기 아까워요.
examples.en: Land in this area is valuable these days, so it feels a shame to sell.

examples.ko: 값나갈 것 같아서 중고 가게에 가져가 봤어요.
examples.en: I thought it might be worth something, so I took it to a secondhand shop.

examples.ko: 예전에 값나가던 물건이 지금은 많이 싸졌어요.
examples.en: Things that used to be worth a lot have become much cheaper now.

explain: '비싸다'는 가격이 높다는 말이고, '값나가다'는 가치가 있어서 값이 꽤 나간다는 느낌으로 물건에 주로 써요. 보통 '값나가는 물건'처럼 꾸미는 형태로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '비싸다' just says the price is high, while '값나가다' suggests an item is worth a good amount because of its value. It is mostly used for objects and often appears as a modifier, as in '값나가는 물건'.

examples.en: I have done business with this bank for a long time.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 십 년 동안 거래했어요.
examples.en: The two companies traded for ten years.

examples.ko: 중고 물건을 직접 만나서 거래하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to meet in person to trade secondhand goods.
There is a way to trade safely.
The shop I deal with has closed.
I paid in cash and got a receipt.

explain: 사고파는 일을 말하는데 가게에서 물건 하나 사는 일에는 잘 안 써요. 회사, 은행, 중고 거래처럼 주고받는 관계가 있을 때 써요. '중고 거래'와 '거래처'를 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It describes buying and selling, but not a single purchase at a shop. It suits ongoing exchanges such as companies, banks and secondhand deals. Learn it with the words for secondhand trade and business partner.

en: ease; reduce (a burden, pain, or cost)

examples.en: The government eases the tax burden on ordinary people.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 허리 통증을 경감해 줘요.
examples.en: This exercise relieves back pain.

examples.ko: 학교가 학생들의 숙제 부담을 경감하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The school decided to lighten the students' homework load.

examples.ko: 약이 증상을 경감하는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The medicine helps ease the symptoms.
I moved somewhere closer to cut costs.
Isn't there a way to ease my parents' worries?

explain: 누가 일부러 부담이나 아픔을 덜 때 써요. '줄이다'보다 딱딱하고, 좋은 쪽으로 덜어 준다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '부담', '통증', '비용' 같은 말과 함께 쓰고, 사람 수나 물건 수를 줄일 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Used when someone deliberately lightens a burden or pain. It is stiffer than 줄이다 and has a feeling of relief. It goes with words like 부담, 통증, and 비용, and is not used for cutting numbers of people or items.

examples.en: Our shop changed its vegetable supplier.

examples.ko: 공급자가 약속한 날짜에 물건을 보내 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: The supplier didn't send the goods on the promised date.

examples.ko: 공급자와 소비자 사이에 가격 차이가 커요.
examples.en: The price gap between supplier and consumer is large.
The supplier wants to raise the price.

examples.ko: 전기 공급자에게 요금 문의 전화를 했어요.
examples.en: I called the electricity provider to ask about the bill.

examples.ko: 부품 공급자 목록을 메일로 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please email me the list of parts suppliers.

explain: 반대 짝은 '소비자'나 '수요자'예요. 회사 일과 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 회사를 말할 때는 '공급업체'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite partners are '소비자' and '수요자'. It comes up often in business and economic news. When talking about a company, '공급업체' is also widely used.

examples.en: This company supplies vegetables to restaurants.
The government supplied masks for free.
The pipe that supplies water burst.
I'm sorry we couldn't supply enough goods.
We will supply electricity to the factory.
We get paid right away when we supply the parts.

explain: 물건, 전기, 물을 계속 대 줄 때 써요. 받는 쪽에서는 '공급받다'라고 해요. 시장에서는 '수요'(필요로 하는 양)와 짝으로 나와요.
explain_en: Use it for continuously providing goods, electricity, or water. From the receiving side you say '공급받다'. In economics it pairs with '수요' (the amount people need).

examples.en: I received the rest after tax was deducted from my pay.
The company deducts insurance premiums from my pay every month.
You can deduct medical expenses in the year-end tax settlement.
I heard donations are also deducted from income.
If you're late, do they deduct a little from your daily wage?
The deducted amount is written on the statement.

explain: 정해진 돈에서 일부를 빼는 것인데, 월급·세금·보험처럼 돈 이야기에서 써요. 가게에서 값을 빼 줄 때는 '깎다', '빼다'라고 해요. '월급에서 세금을 공제하다'처럼 '에서'와 '을/를'을 함께 써요.
explain_en: It means taking a part out of a set sum and is used in money talk such as pay, taxes and insurance. When a shop lowers the price people say '깎다' or '빼다'. It is used with both '에서' and '을/를', as in '월급에서 세금을 공제하다'.

examples.ko: 관람료는 어른 오천 원, 어린이 삼천 원이에요.
examples.en: Admission is 5,000 won for adults and 3,000 won for children.
This exhibition has no admission fee.
Pay the admission fee at the entrance and get your ticket.
Students only pay half the admission fee.
I was surprised that the museum admission fee went up a lot.
Is the price of a drink included in the admission fee?

explain: 영화, 전시, 공연처럼 '보는' 것에 내는 돈에 어울려요. '입장료'는 놀이공원이나 공원처럼 '들어가는' 값이라 둘이 겹칠 때도 있어요. 말할 때는 그냥 '표값'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It fits money paid to watch things like movies, exhibitions and performances. '입장료' is the price for entering places such as theme parks, and the two sometimes overlap. In casual speech people also just say '표값'.

examples.ko: 이 서점은 책 구색이 좋아서 자주 와요.
examples.en: This bookstore has a good selection of books, so I come often.

examples.ko: 구색을 제대로 갖추려면 비용이 꽤 들어요.
examples.en: It costs quite a lot to put together a proper assortment.

examples.ko: 구색만 갖춘 행사라서 별로 기대가 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's an event that only goes through the motions, so I don't expect much.

examples.ko: 작은 가게지만 구색은 웬만한 마트 못지않아요.
examples.en: It's a small shop, but its range is just as good as many supermarkets.

examples.ko: 선물 구색 맞추기로 넣은 물건이라 잘 안 팔려요.
examples.en: It was added just to round out the gift lineup, so it doesn't sell well.

examples.ko: 구색에 신경 써서 다양한 음료를 준비했어요.
examples.en: I paid attention to variety and prepared many different drinks.

explain: '구색을 갖추다', '구색을 맞추다'처럼 여러 종류를 고루 갖춘다는 느낌으로 써요. '구색만 갖추다'는 알맹이 없이 겉모양만 맞췄다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 가게의 상품 종류가 다양할 때 '구색이 좋다'고 말해요.
explain_en: It appears in set phrases like '구색을 갖추다' and '구색을 맞추다', with the feel of having a well-rounded variety. '구색만 갖추다' has a negative tone: only the outward form is there, with nothing substantial. For a shop with a wide range of goods, people say '구색이 좋다'.

examples.ko: 가게 양도 계약서를 쓰기 전에 권리금부터 확인하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Before signing the shop transfer contract, it's best to check the key money first.

examples.ko: 이 자리는 권리금이 너무 비싸서 포기했어요.
examples.en: The key money for this spot was too expensive, so I gave up.

examples.ko: 권리금을 못 받고 가게를 닫는 사장님도 있어요.
examples.en: Some owners close their shops without getting any key money.

examples.ko: 권리금은 보증금과 달리 건물주에게 내는 돈이 아니에요.
examples.en: Unlike a deposit, key money isn't paid to the building owner.

examples.ko: 권리금 없는 가게를 찾아서 계속 보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm still looking for a shop with no key money.

examples.ko: 권리금으로 삼천만 원을 주고 가게를 넘겨받았어요.
examples.en: I took over the shop by paying thirty million won in key money.

explain: 가게를 넘겨받을 때 이전 가게 주인에게 주는 돈이라서, 건물주에게 내는 '보증금'과 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요. 보증금은 나중에 돌려받지만 권리금은 보통 돌려받기 어려워요.
explain_en: This is money paid to the previous shop owner when you take over a business, so don't confuse it with '보증금' (deposit), which goes to the landlord. A deposit is returned later, but key money is usually hard to get back.

examples.en: Because of moving, I put my house up for a quick sale.
Urgent-sale items come out cheaper than the market price.
I went to see a car that was listed for a quick sale.
I asked the real estate agent if there were any urgent sales.

examples.ko: 급매 물건이라도 꼼꼼히 확인하고 사야 해요.
examples.en: Even for an urgent-sale item, you should check carefully before buying.

examples.ko: 빨리 팔려고 가격을 내려서 급매로 올렸어요.
examples.en: To sell quickly, I lowered the price and listed it as an urgent sale.

explain: 집이나 차를 급하게 팔아야 해서 값을 낮추어 내놓는 거래예요. 부동산 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 그런 물건은 '급매물'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a sale where the seller needs to sell fast and lowers the price. It appears often in real estate talk, and such items are also called '급매물'.

examples.en: I suddenly needed cash quickly, so I asked a friend.
I'm worried because I have nowhere to borrow quick cash from.

examples.ko: 월말에는 급전 때문에 고민하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: At the end of the month, many people worry about needing cash fast.
Quick loans have high interest, so be careful.

examples.ko: 아버지가 급전으로 쓸 돈을 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father sent me money to use in an emergency.
Can you lend me some quick cash?

explain: '급전이 필요하다', '급전을 구하다', '급전을 융통하다'처럼 써요. 당장 필요해서 짧게 빌리는 돈이라는 느낌이 있어요. 미리 모아 둔 '비상금'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '급전이 필요하다' and '급전을 구하다'. It carries the feel of money needed right now and borrowed for a short time. It differs from '비상금', which is money you have saved in advance.

examples.ko: 선반 위 상자를 조심히 끌어내려 주세요.
examples.en: Please carefully pull the box down from the shelf.
My little brother didn't want to get up, so I pulled his blanket off.
I pulled my hat down to my eyes.
The government is trying to bring prices down.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에 있는 가방을 끌어내리다가 떨어뜨렸어요.
examples.en: I was pulling down a bag from a high place and dropped it.
The store lowered its prices, and more customers came.

explain: 위에 있는 것을 잡아당겨 아래로 내리는 동작이에요. 물건뿐 아니라 가격, 점수, 순위를 낮출 때도 써요. 반대말은 '끌어올리다'예요.
explain_en: It means pulling something from above down to a lower position. Besides objects, it is also used for lowering prices, scores or rankings. The opposite is '끌어올리다'.

en: be sold to a bidder; be auctioned

examples.ko: 낙찰된 업체는 열흘 안에 계약서를 내야 해요.
examples.en: The company awarded the bid must submit the contract within ten days.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 제안이 낙찰됐다는 소식에 팀원들이 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: All the team members were happy to hear our proposal had won the bid.
That painting was sold at auction for 200 million won.

examples.ko: 가장 낮은 가격을 낸 곳이 낙찰돼요.
examples.en: The one that offers the lowest price gets the bid.

examples.ko: 어제 온라인 경매에서 시계가 낙찰되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The watch wasn't sold in yesterday's online auction.

examples.ko: 공사가 낙찰되면 바로 일을 시작할 거예요.
examples.en: Once the construction project is awarded, we will start work right away.

explain: 경매에서는 물건이 팔릴 때, 입찰에서는 사업이나 공사가 어느 한 곳으로 정해질 때 써요. 사람이 주어이면 '낙찰받다'를 많이 쓰고, 입찰이 성립하지 않은 경우는 '유찰되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: For auctions it means an item gets sold, and for tenders it means a project is awarded to one bidder. When a person or company is the subject, '낙찰받다' is often used, and a failed tender is '유찰되다'.

examples.ko: 학교 납부금은 다음 주까지 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay the school fees by next week.

examples.ko: 이번 학기 납부금을 은행에서 내도 돼요?
examples.en: Can I pay this semester's fees at the bank?

examples.ko: 이번 달 납부금이 얼마인지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how much the fee is this month.
I lost my fee receipt. What should I do?
The fees include the school meal cost too.
I paid the fees with the scholarship money.

explain: '내는 돈'보다 딱딱한 말이라 학교 안내문이나 고지서에서 자주 보여요. 학교에서는 등록금, 급식비 같은 여러 가지 돈을 묶어서 말할 때 써요. 함께 쓰는 말은 '납부하다', '고지서'예요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than 'money you pay' and often appears in school notices and bills. Schools use it to group together various payments such as tuition and meal fees. Common partners are '납부하다' (to pay) and '고지서' (bill).

examples.en: Our factory supplies parts to a large company.
We have to deliver the products by tomorrow.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 학교에 급식 재료를 납품했어요.
examples.en: That company supplied food ingredients to the school.
We loaded the goods to be delivered onto the truck.

examples.ko: 싼 가격에 납품하는 업체를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a company that supplies at a low price.

examples.ko: 납품하고 나면 대금을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once we deliver, we can get paid.

explain: 주문한 회사나 기관에 물건을 가져다줄 때 써요. 회사끼리의 거래라서 개인에게 보내는 '배송하다', '배달하다'와 달라요. 돈은 보통 납품한 뒤에 받아요. 받는 쪽에서는 '납품받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when bringing goods to the company or organization that ordered them. It is a business-to-business matter, so it differs from '배송하다' or '배달하다', which go to individuals. Payment usually comes after delivery. From the receiving side it is '납품받다'.

examples.ko: 회사는 사업 다각화를 위해 새 분야에 투자했어요.
examples.en: The company invested in a new field to diversify its business.

examples.ko: 수출 시장 다각화가 필요하다는 말이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say export markets need to be diversified.

examples.ko: 농가는 소득 다각화를 위해 체험 프로그램도 운영해요.
examples.en: Farms also run experience programs to diversify their income.
Diversifying your investments is important to reduce risk.

examples.ko: 다각화에 성공한 기업은 불황에도 잘 버텼어요.
examples.en: Companies that succeeded in diversifying held up well even in the downturn.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 메뉴 다각화로 손님이 늘었어요.
examples.en: This shop got more customers by diversifying its menu.

explain: '사업 다각화', '투자 다각화'처럼 경제 뉴스나 수업에서 많이 나와요. '다각화를 추진하다', '다각화를 꾀하다'처럼 써요. '다변화'와 겹치는 부분이 많아서 비슷한 상황에서 둘 다 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It appears in economic news and lessons, as in '사업 다각화' and '투자 다각화'. It is used in phrases like '다각화를 추진하다' and '다각화를 꾀하다'. It overlaps a lot with '다변화', so you may see both in similar situations.

examples.ko: 새 길이 생겨서 출근 시간을 단축했어요.
examples.en: A new road opened, so I cut my commute time.
The company decided to shorten working hours.

examples.ko: 이 앱을 쓰면 공부 시간을 단축할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this app you can cut down your study time.

examples.ko: 공사 기간을 단축해서 다음 달에 열어요.
examples.en: They shortened the construction period and will open next month.
The plane shortened our travel time.
I sent the materials in advance to shorten the meeting.

explain: 단축하다는 시간이나 기간, 거리를 짧게 줄일 때 써요. '시간을 단축하다', '기간을 단축하다'처럼 시간 관련 말과 가장 잘 어울려요. 글자 수나 양을 줄일 때는 '줄이다'를 더 자연스럽게 써요.
explain_en: 단축하다 is used for making time, a period, or a distance shorter. It pairs best with words like '시간' and '기간', as in '시간을 단축하다'. For cutting the amount or number of something, '줄이다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: You need collateral to get a loan from the bank.
I put up my house as collateral and borrowed money.

examples.ko: 담보물의 가치가 떨어지면 대출이 어려워질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the value of the collateral drops, getting a loan can become difficult.

examples.ko: 빚을 갚지 못하면 담보물을 처분할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't repay the debt, the collateral may be sold off.

examples.ko: 담보물 없이 빌릴 수 있는 대출도 있어요.
examples.en: There are also loans you can get without collateral.
I submitted the list of collateral to the bank.

explain: '담보'는 빚을 갚을 수 있다는 보장 자체를 말하고, '담보물'은 그 보장으로 실제로 맡기는 물건(집, 땅 등)을 가리켜요. 은행 대출이나 금융 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '담보' refers to the guarantee itself that a debt will be repaid, while '담보물' is the actual item (a house, land, etc.) put up for it. It often appears in bank loans and financial news.

en: put up as collateral; mortgage; guarantee, ensure

examples.ko: 이 대출은 집을 담보하는 조건으로 받았어요.
examples.en: I got this loan on the condition of putting up my house as collateral.
It's a device that guarantees safety.

examples.ko: 품질을 담보할 수 있는 회사만 선택했어요.
examples.en: I only chose companies that can guarantee quality.
There is no method that guarantees success.
Using my car as collateral made the loan easy.
This system guarantees students' rights.

explain: 은행에서 집이나 차를 맡기고 돈을 빌릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. 요즘은 '안전을 담보하다'처럼 어떤 일이 꼭 되도록 보장한다는 쪽으로 더 자주 들려요. 뉴스와 글에서 '~을/를 담보하지 못하다'처럼 부정형도 많이 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 맡긴다는 원래 뜻에서 넓어져, 어떤 결과를 믿고 맡길 수 있게 보장한다는 뜻으로 써요. 뉴스와 글에서 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Extended from the original idea of pledging something, it means ensuring a result you can rely on. Common in news and writing.

explain_en: At a bank it means putting up a house or car as collateral for a loan. These days you more often hear the sense of making sure something happens, as in '안전을 담보하다'. In news and writing, the negative '~을/를 담보하지 못하다' is also very common.

examples.en: I borrowed comic books from the neighborhood rental shop.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에 비디오 대여점이 있었어요.
examples.en: There used to be a video rental shop in front of my house.

examples.ko: 캠핑 장비는 대여점에 가면 싸게 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can rent camping gear cheaply if you go to a rental shop.
This rental shop is closed on Sundays.
There are many hanbok rental shops near tourist spots.
The owner of the rental shop recommended a book to me.

explain: 물건을 빌려주는 가게예요. 앞에 '만화책, 비디오, 한복, 캠핑 장비'처럼 빌려주는 물건을 붙여서 말해요. 요즘은 '렌탈샵'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a shop that lends things out. You put the item before it, like '만화책, 비디오, 한복, 캠핑 장비'. These days people also say '렌탈샵'.

examples.en: Detergent is much cheaper if you buy it in bulk.

examples.ko: 이 샴푸는 대용량이라 몇 달 동안 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This shampoo is a large size, so it lasts for months.
It's hard to send large files by email.
Since I live alone, small packages are more convenient than bulk ones.

examples.ko: 이 보조 배터리는 대용량인데도 가볍고 작아요.
examples.en: This power bank is high-capacity but still light and small.

examples.ko: 마트에서 대용량 과자를 사 왔더니 너무 많아요.
examples.en: I bought a big bag of snacks at the mart and it's too much.

explain: '대용량 세제', '대용량 배터리', '대용량 파일'처럼 물건의 양이나 저장 용량이 큰 것을 말해요. 반대는 '소용량'이에요. 마트에서는 '대용량 포장', 컴퓨터에서는 '대용량 파일'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for things with a large amount or storage capacity, as in '대용량 세제', '대용량 배터리' and '대용량 파일'. The opposite is '소용량'. You see it as '대용량 포장' (bulk packaging) at the mart and '대용량 파일' on computers.

examples.en: This wholesaler only sells fruit by the box.

examples.ko: 시장에 도매상이 모여 있는 골목이 있어요.
examples.en: The market has an alley where wholesalers are gathered.
Buying from a wholesaler is much cheaper than at a store.
My father runs a stationery wholesale business.
I get goods from a wholesaler and pass them on to retail shops.

examples.ko: 새벽에 도매상까지 가서 꽃을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I went all the way to the wholesaler at dawn and bought flowers.

explain: 물건을 많이 사서 가게에 넘기는 가게나 사람이에요. 반대말은 '소매상'이고, 가격 이야기에서는 '도매가'처럼 쓰여요. 보통 손님 한 명에게 팔지 않고 가게 주인에게 팔아요.
explain_en: It is a shop or person that buys goods in bulk and sells them on to other stores. The opposite is '소매상' (retailer), and in price talk you hear '도매가' (wholesale price). It usually sells to shop owners, not to individual customers.

en: monopolizing; take-it-all; having something to oneself

examples.ko: 우리 사회가 승자 독식 구조라는 비판이 많아요.
examples.en: There is a lot of criticism that our society has a winner-takes-all structure.
To prevent profits from being monopolized, we need rules.
Complaints are piling up because of the monopolizing.

examples.ko: 그 팀의 독식 현상에 다른 팀들이 불만을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The other teams complained about that team taking everything.
Monopolizing ends up hurting everyone.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에서는 한 나라의 메달 독식이 깨졌어요.
examples.en: In this tournament, one country's sweep of the medals was broken.

explain: '승자 독식'이라는 표현으로 가장 많이 만나요. 뉴스나 글에서 쓰는 한자어라서 일상 대화에서는 '독차지'나 '혼자 다 가지다'가 자연스러워요. 동사로는 '독식하다'를 써요.
explain_en: You will meet it most often in the expression '승자 독식' (winner takes all). It is a Sino-Korean word used in news and writing, so in daily conversation '독차지' or '혼자 다 가지다' sounds more natural. The verb form is '독식하다'.

en: offer remainder at a cheap price

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 문 닫기 전에 남은 빵을 떨이해요.
examples.en: The shop owner sells off the leftover bread before closing.

examples.ko: 재고를 떨이하려고 큰 폭으로 값을 내렸어요.
examples.en: They cut the price a lot to clear out the stock.

examples.ko: 시장 상인이 오후에 남은 생선을 떨이했어요.
examples.en: The market vendor sold off the remaining fish in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 저녁 시간에는 도시락을 떨이하는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many places sell off their lunch boxes cheaply in the evening.
I hope we can sell all of it off cheaply today.

examples.ko: 안 팔린 옷을 떨이해서 창고를 비웠어요.
examples.en: We sold the unsold clothes at clearance prices and emptied the warehouse.

explain: 팔다 남은 물건을 싸게 처분하는 행동이에요. 보통 파는 사람이 주어이고, '떨이로 팔다'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요. 재고를 빨리 없애려는 상황에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the act of disposing of leftover goods at a low price. The subject is usually the seller, and people also say it as '떨이로 팔다'. It is used in situations where stock needs to be cleared quickly.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 유행을 타고 떼돈을 벌었대요.
examples.en: I heard that shop made a fortune riding the trend.

examples.ko: 주식으로 떼돈을 번 사람은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people make a fortune from stocks.

examples.ko: 형이 장사로 떼돈을 벌더니 새 집으로 이사했어요.
examples.en: My brother made a killing in business and moved into a new house.

examples.ko: 한 번에 떼돈 벌 생각만 하면 위험해요.
examples.en: It's risky to think only about getting rich all at once.

examples.ko: 옆집 아저씨는 김밥 장사로 떼돈을 번 뒤에 가게를 하나 더 열었어요.
examples.en: The man next door made a fortune selling gimbap and then opened another shop.

examples.ko: 저는 떼돈보다 안정적인 월급이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer a stable salary over a big fortune.

explain: '큰돈'보다 구어적이고, 장사나 투자처럼 한꺼번에 크게 버는 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 주로 '떼돈을 벌다' 꼴로 써요. 돈을 많이 쓴다고 할 때는 '큰돈을 쓰다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is more colloquial than '큰돈' and suits stories of earning a lot at once through business or investing. It is mainly used as '떼돈을 벌다'. To say someone spent a lot, '큰돈을 쓰다' is more natural.
